[[File:Amabe Clan genealogy.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Genealogy of the Amabe Clan (Main Genealogy)]]
The '''Genealogy of the Amabe Clan''' (海部氏系図, Amabe-shi Keizu) is a genealogy passed down by the [[Amabe clan]] (海部氏, Amabe-shi), the shrine family (社家, Shake) of [[Kono Shrine]] (籠神社, {{ill|Kono Shrine|en|Kono Shrine|qid=Q705126|lt=Kono Shrine}}), located in {{ill|Miyazu|en|Miyazu|qid=Q111018930|lt=Miyazu}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|qid=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture}}. It consists of two volumes: the '''Genealogy of the Shrine Priests of Kono Shrine''' (籠名神社祝部氏係図, Main Genealogy) and the '''Annotated Genealogy of the Shrine Priests of Kono Shrine, Amabe Clan of Tanba Province''' (籠名神宮祝部丹波国造海部直等氏之本記, Annotated Genealogy).
Both genealogies are valuable documents for studying the evolution of ancient clan and ritual systems. They were designated as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} in {{ill|1975|en|1975|qid=Q2479|lt=1975}} and as {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|en|National Treasure (Japan)|qid=Q1139795|lt=National Treasure (Japan)}} in {{ill|1976|en|1976|qid=Q2480|lt=1976}} <ref group="note">The "Annotated Genealogy" was designated as an "accompanying item" (附).</ref>.
== Main Genealogy ==
The "Main Genealogy" is among the oldest genealogies in Japan, second only to the {{ill|Enchin Genealogy|ja|円珍俗姓系図|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchin Genealogy|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, part of the {{ill|Chisho Daishi-related Documents|ja|智証大師関係文書典籍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chisho Daishi-related Documents|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, also known as the "Genealogy of the Waki Clan" (和気氏系図). <ref group="note">The "Genealogy of the Waki Clan" was completed by the early Shōwa period (9th century).</ref> As a vertical genealogy, it is considered a rare relic that best preserves the ancient form of genealogies.
The genealogy is a scroll (巻子, Makimono) made of five sheets of mulberry paper (楮紙, Kōzo-shi) joined together, measuring 25.7 cm wide and 228.5 cm long. The title at the center reads "Tanba Province, Yosa District, Kono Shrine, Descendants of the Amabe Clan," followed by a single line of light ink under which the names of deities and people are written. Each name is accompanied by a red square seal marked "Tanba Province." This indicates that the genealogy was submitted to and approved by the Tanba Provincial Office.
The genealogy is dated between June 8, 871 CE (when the Kono Shrine was promoted to junior fourth Rank) and December 14, 877 CE (when it was promoted to junior fourth Rank, upper). <ref group="note">Kono Shrine was promoted to junior fourth Rank on June 8, 871, and to junior fourth Rank, upper, on December 14, 877, according to the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}.</ref> It is believed to have been compiled by the 33rd head of the family, Amabe-no-Atai Inao (海部直稲雄). <ref group="note">The "Annotated Genealogy" attributes the compilation to the 32nd head, Tadao, but notes indicate he served as a shrine priest (祝, Hōri) until 864, which creates a chronological inconsistency.</ref>
=== Content ===
The genealogy consists of three parts:
* From the progenitor [[Hikohoakari no Mikoto]] to the 19th head, Takeshibune no Sukune (建振熊宿祢), covering the period before family names (kabane) were used. This section is sparse, with large gaps.
* From the 20th head, Tobi (都比), to the 24th head, Kunini (勲尼), during the period when the clan held the title "Amabe-no-Atai" and managed the maritime communities (海人族, Ama) in {{ill|Tanba Province|en|Tanba Province|qid=Q954511|lt=Tanba Province}}.
* From the 25th head, Gobekimichi (伍佰道), to the 32nd head, Tadao, during the "shrine priest era," with the title "Amabe-no-Atai" and service at the Kono Shrine. The genealogy records each head's years of service.
== Annotated Genealogy ==
The "Annotated Genealogy" is a more detailed version of the "Main Genealogy," annotated with additional notes. The existing copy is an early {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}} manuscript, with an afterword by the scribe, Amabe Katsu Chiyo (海部勝千代). The original text, dated to the {{ill|Ninna|en|Ninna|qid=Q1346317|lt=Ninna era}} (885–889 CE), is known as the "Genealogy of the Amabe Clan of Tanba Province."
The manuscript was written on reused paper containing illustrations of weather predictions and omens from the late {{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|en|Azuchi–Momoyama period|qid=Q319531|lt=Azuchi–Momoyama period}}, which adds historical value. The annotations trace the origins of the Amabe clan, provide details missing from the "Main Genealogy," and include unique legends not found in other records such as the {{ill|Kiki (Shinto)|ja|記紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q842308}} or the {{ill|Kujiki|ja|旧事本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kojiki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q2716751}}.
=== Content ===
The "Annotated Genealogy" traces the lineage from the progenitor to the 34th head, providing additional details about each person's deeds and noting collateral lines and their descendants.
== Historical Evaluation ==
The genealogy has been studied by historians such as [[Masashi Murata]], [[Toshihide Akamatsu]], and [[Nobuyoshi Yamamoto]]. Despite minimal skepticism or criticism, historian [[Ryō Ōta]] raised a concern about the absence of Amabe no Oshitatatsu (海直忍立), who is mentioned in other historical records.
